Aggregate per-cell CP10K counts of S and G1 cells over several samples

Source: R/pseudobulk.R
aggregate_pseudobulk_s_g1_counts.Rd

Takes one raw genome-bin count matrix per sample, normalises every selected cell to counts per 10,000 (the denominator is the cell's total over all raw bins, before any mappability filter) and sums the normalised counts per bin over the QC-passed S cells (is_G1 is FALSE and pass_qc is TRUE) and over the G1 cells (is_G1 is TRUE).

Usage

aggregate_pseudobulk_s_g1_counts(genobins, meta_data, bin_ids, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

genobins

A sparse bins x cells count matrix, or a list of them (one per sample; the names, if any, are the sample ids).

meta_data

A data.frame with cell ids as row names and logical columns is_G1 and pass_qc.

bin_ids

Character vector of bin ids. Each matrix must have exactly these row names (rows are reordered if needed).

verbose

Print one message per sample. Default FALSE.

Value

A data.frame with columns bin_id, s_counts and g1_counts (summed CP10K, not raw reads), and attributes normalization ("cp10k_per_cell_v1") and selected_cells (cells used per sample).

Details

When genobins is a named list, cell names of a matrix that do not start with "<sample>-" get that prefix before they are matched to rownames(meta_data); a single matrix (or an unnamed list) is matched as is. Every cell of every matrix must be present in meta_data, and each matrix must contribute at least one S cell and one G1 cell.

To start from the per-sample RDS files, read them first, e.g. lapply(files, readRDS) with a named files vector.

See also

calculate_pseudobulk_rt_g1_ratio(), export_pseudobulk_g1_ratio()
